sections.h2: Where is Oxford, Mississippi, and what shapes its housing?
sections.html:
Oxford is the county seat of Lafayette County in north Mississippi, about 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis. It is a college town built around the University of Mississippi, known as Ole Miss, and its 2020 census population was 25,416.

The city lies in the North Central Hills, a region of forested ridges and red clay. Downtown sits on one ridge and the university campus on another, while the main commercial corridors run through the valleys between them. On a hilly lot with red clay, drainage and grading are worth checking before you list.

Oxford is where highways from eight directions meet. Mississippi Highway 6, which also carries U.S. 278, runs west to Batesville and east to Pontotoc. Highway 7 runs north to Holly Springs and south to Water Valley, and Highway 30 heads northeast toward New Albany.

sections.h2: How does Ole Miss affect selling a house in Oxford?
sections.html:
The university is the largest single influence on Oxford's housing, and it is why the city's numbers look different from the rest of north Mississippi. The median age is 27.8 years, only 19.8 percent of households have children under 18, and nearly 44 percent of households are one person.

Ole Miss reported 28,960 students across all its campuses in fall 2026, a 2 percent increase and its fourth straight record. The class of first-time freshmen was 5,363 students, the third largest ever. Growth like that is why rentals and investor-owned houses make up a notable share of the market.

The census shows a 25.6 percent vacancy rate for housing units and a 19.7 percent rental vacancy rate, both high for a city of this size. If you own a rental, check your lease end dates against your target closing date.

The campus itself, known as University, Mississippi, is an unincorporated area that the city of Oxford fully surrounds.

  • Owner-occupants selling a family home usually follow a normal listing path.
  • Landlords with student tenants should review lease end dates before choosing a closing date.
  • Heirs of a house that needs work may prefer a quick as-is sale.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Oxford's older neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Oxford was founded in 1837 when three pioneers bought land from a Chickasaw landowner, and it was named after Oxford, England to promote it as a center of learning. The Mississippi legislature chose it in 1841 as the site of the state university, which opened in 1848.

Union troops occupied the town in 1862, and in 1864 buildings around the square, including the county courthouse, were burned. A new courthouse was built in 1872. After the war, freedmen settled in a neighborhood known as Freedmen Town, where they built houses, businesses, churches and schools.

Oxford is also the home of novelist William Faulkner, whose house, Rowan Oak, is a landmark. Ammadelle, an 1859 mansion, was designed by Calvert Vaux, who co-designed Central Park. The city publishes Oxford Historic Design Guidelines, so owners of older houses in historic areas should read them before exterior changes and tell buyers about any approvals.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Oxford's streets, transit and services?
sections.html:
Downtown Oxford follows a grid with a distinctive naming pattern. Many north-south streets are numbered from west to east, starting at the old railroad depot, while east-west avenues are named for presidents in order from Washington to Cleveland. Lamar Boulevard replaces what would be Twelfth Street, and University Avenue takes the place of Polk Avenue.

The city runs a bus service called Oxford-University Transit, with routes around town and across campus. Ole Miss students and faculty ride free with university identification. University-Oxford Airport, owned by the university, is about two nautical miles northwest of the central business district.

Baptist Memorial Hospital North Mississippi is in Oxford, and Oxford Utilities and the city's environmental services and recycling departments handle services. The city is served by two public school districts: the Oxford School District, which covers most of the area, and the Lafayette County School District, which covers small outlying sections. Private options include Oxford University School, Regents School of Oxford and Magnolia Montessori.

sections.h2: What building and permit rules apply in Oxford?
sections.html:
Oxford's Building division administers building, electrical, mechanical, plumbing and fuel gas codes and erosion control ordinances. It accepts residential and commercial permit applications, performs inspections and issues certificates of occupancy or completion. The city is moving permit applications and inspection scheduling to an online system called EnerGov.

Current city codes include the 2024 International Building Code, the 2024 International Residential Code (with local changes), the 2023 National Electrical Code, and the 2024 plumbing, mechanical, fuel gas and fire codes. The city also publishes a building permit fee schedule and a 2026 permit fee chart.

If you renovated without a permit, a buyer's inspector may ask for the file. For a hilly lot, the erosion control ordinance is worth reading, because grading and clearing can trigger requirements. A cash buyer will often take a house with open permit questions, but you should still disclose what you know.

The City of Oxford posts its rules on its Building and Development page, and all city ordinances are on Municode.

sections.h2: How do Lafayette County property taxes work for a seller?
sections.html:
Lafayette County bills the tax, due by February 1 of each year. Payments can be made at the office, by phone or online. The county's page notes that debit and credit cards carry a 2.35 percent fee.

Mississippi assesses a single-family, owner-occupied home at 10 percent of its true value and other real property at 15 percent, so a rental house is taxed on a higher share of value than an owner's home. The state says that real property must be revalued at least every four years and that an owner who disagrees can request a hearing before the Board of Supervisors, usually by the first Monday in August.

A house inside Oxford pays a county rate, a school district rate and a city rate. The assessment date is January 1, so the owner of record on that date receives the bill. Your closing agent will normally split the year between you and the buyer.

Homestead exemption applications go to the tax assessor between January 1 and April 1. The state notes that a change in ownership or occupancy can require a new application, which matters when a student-area house changes from a rental to an owner-occupied home. Taxes left unpaid can end in a county tax sale, so pay or arrange payoff before closing.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Oxford?
sections.html:
Oxford sellers can list with an agent, sell privately or accept a cash offer. Because the market is shaped by the university, the best path depends on who owns the house and what shape it is in. A renovated home near campus may draw interest through a listing. An inherited house with deferred repairs may fit a cash sale better.

Mississippi law requires most sellers to deliver a written property condition disclosure statement before title transfers (Mississippi Code section 89-1-503). A buyer who receives it late has three days after in-person delivery, or five after mailing, to cancel the offer.

faqs.q: How far is Oxford, MS from Memphis?
faqs.a: Oxford is about 75 miles south-southeast of Memphis, Tennessee. Highway 6 and Highway 7 are the main routes into the city.

faqs.q: How many students attend Ole Miss?
faqs.a: The University of Mississippi reported 28,960 students across all its campuses in fall 2026, a 2 percent increase and its fourth straight enrollment record.

faqs.q: When are Lafayette County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Property taxes are due by February 1 each year. They can be paid at the tax collector's office, by phone or online, and card payments carry a 2.35 percent fee.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for renovations in Oxford, MS?
faqs.a: Oxford's Building division issues residential and commercial permits and performs inspections. Contact the city to confirm whether your project needs one.
The Oxford School District serves most of the city, and the Lafayette County School District serves small outlying sections.

faqs.q: Does Mississippi require a seller disclosure form?
faqs.a: In most sales, yes. Section 89-1-503 requires delivery before title transfers. If it comes after an offer, the buyer has three days in person or five days by mail to cancel.

faqs.q: Can I sell a student rental in Oxford for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers often purchase rentals as-is. Check your lease end dates and the tenants' rights before choosing a closing date.
